content: 1. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce pyridoxine levels by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 2. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens increase ropinirole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 3. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease rose hips levels by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 4. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the therapeutic effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and associated adverse effects. This interaction requires close monitoring. 5. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients, as estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic agents. 6. Ambrisentan increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 7. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 8. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the potential for reduced efficacy. 10. Androstenedione increases the effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 11. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 12. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of argatroban through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 14. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 15. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 16. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease ascorbic acid levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 17. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended, and alternative options should be considered if available. 18. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 19. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease axitinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 20. Azithromycin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 21. Aztreonam decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 22. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of bemiparin and bivalirudin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 23. Boron increases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 24. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 25. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 26. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 27. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by increasing metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Close monitoring is recommended. 28. Cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefamandole, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, and cephalexin decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. An additional or alternative form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 29. Chloramphenicol and chlorhexidine oral decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 30. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 31. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and decreases their levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification or alternative drugs should be considered. Close monitoring is recommended. 33. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 34. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens interact with clomipramine through an unspecified mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the therapeutic effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and associated adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 35. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 36. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 37. Cortisone decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 38. Crofelemer increases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 and transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 39. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease cyanocobalamin levels by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor.
